labs.title: Configure an eligible role assignment in Privileged Identity Management
labs.summary: Use Microsoft Entra PIM to grant just-in-time eligibility, require MFA and approval for activation, and audit the simulated activation request.
labs.scenario: Contoso's service operations team occasionally needs to update user profiles and group membership, but they should not hold standing administrative access. In the **simulated Microsoft Entra admin center** on your lab VM, use **Privileged Identity Management** to make **Mei Chen** eligible for the **User Administrator** role for a time-bound assignment. Configure the role settings so activation is limited, requires MFA, requires justification, and requires approval from the **Security Approvers** group. Then simulate Mei activating the role with a business justification and review the audit history. Do not create a permanent active assignment.
learningObjectives: Explain just-in-time and just-enough administration in Microsoft Entra PIM
Create an eligible, time-bound role assignment instead of standing active access
Configure activation controls such as MFA, justification, and approval
prerequisites: Know that Zero Trust assumes breach and verifies each privileged action

components.text: Privileged Identity Management supports **Zero Trust** by reducing standing access. Eligible assignments are **just-in-time**: the user must activate the role when needed. Role settings enforce **just-enough** controls such as MFA, justification, approval, and activation duration.

steps.title: Open the User Administrator role in PIM
steps.instruction: Go to **Privileged Identity Management** under **ID Governance**, open **Microsoft Entra roles**, and select **User Administrator** from **Roles**.
steps.hint: PIM role pages are separate from ordinary Roles & admins because they manage eligible and active privileged access.
steps.explanation: PIM supports just-in-time administration: a user can be eligible for a role without holding the permissions all day.

rules.description: The User Administrator PIM role page was opened

steps.title: Add a time-bound eligible assignment
steps.instruction: Select **+ Add assignments** and assign **User Administrator** to **Mei Chen**. Set **Assignment type** to **Eligible** and **Assignment duration** to **Time-bound** ending after **6 months**. Add the provided business justification and select **Assign**.
steps.hint: Eligible means Mei must activate the role before using it. Active would grant standing access immediately.
steps.explanation: Time-bound eligible assignments reduce long-term privileged exposure and support Zero Trust by verifying privileged actions when needed.

rules.description: Mei has eligible time-bound User Administrator access
rules.failureFeedback: Create an eligible, time-bound User Administrator assignment for Mei Chen.

steps.title: Require strong activation controls
steps.instruction: Open **Role settings** for **User Administrator**. Set **Activation maximum duration (hours)** to `4`, turn on **On activation, require multifactor authentication**, **Require justification on activation**, and **Require approval to activate**, then choose **Security Approvers** and select **Update**.
steps.hint: Role settings apply to every activation for that role.
steps.explanation: MFA verifies the user, justification records why privilege is needed, and approval adds human oversight before elevation.

rules.description: User Administrator activation requires MFA, justification, approval, and a short duration
rules.failureFeedback: Update User Administrator role settings to require MFA, justification, approval by Security Approvers, and 4 hours maximum.

steps.title: Simulate activation with justification
steps.instruction: Open **My roles**, activate **User Administrator** for **2** hours, confirm **MFA requirement satisfied in simulation**, enter the business justification, and use **Approved by Security Approvers**.
steps.hint: This is a simulation. Do not add sign-in steps; activation happens inside the lab state.
steps.explanation: Activation is the just-in-time step. The audit trail should show who activated what role, why, and under which controls.

rules.description: Mei activated User Administrator with MFA, approval, and justification
rules.failureFeedback: Activate the eligible User Administrator role with MFA satisfied, approval, and justification.

steps.title: Review the audit history
steps.instruction: Open **Audit history** and confirm that the assignment, role settings update, and activation events are recorded.
steps.hint: Audit history is part of privileged access governance and supports later access reviews.
steps.explanation: PIM audit evidence helps administrators review privileged access and investigate unexpected activation.

rules.description: The activation appears in audit history
rules.failureFeedback: Review Audit history after activating the role.

labs.solution:
1. Select **Privileged Identity Management** > **Microsoft Entra roles** > **Roles**, then open **User Administrator**.
2. Select **+ Add assignments**. Choose **User Administrator** and **Mei Chen**. In **Membership settings**, set **Assignment type** to **Eligible**, **Assignment duration** to **Time-bound**, **Ends after** to **6 months**, enter the justification, and select **Assign**.
3. Open **Role settings** for **User Administrator**. Set **Activation maximum duration (hours)** to `4`, turn on **On activation, require multifactor authentication**, **Require justification on activation**, and **Require approval to activate**. Choose **Security Approvers**, then **Update**.
4. Open **My roles**, activate **User Administrator** for `2` hours, keep **MFA requirement satisfied in simulation** on, enter the justification, choose **Approved by Security Approvers**, and select **Activate**.
5. Open **Audit history** and review the assignment, settings update, and activation records.
6. Do not use **Active** or **Permanent** for Mei. The objective is just-in-time and just-enough access.
